newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan foes fight near Kabul, claim victories.
newsitem.headline: Afghan foes fight near Kabul, claim victories.

text.p: The Afghan government and its rival Taleban Islamic militia claimed victories against each other on Saturday in renewed fighting near the capital and in the east.
Government troops seized eight positions and killed 15 Taleban fighters in an assault southwest of Kabul backed by jet bombing and artillery, official Kabul Radio said.

Taleban spokesmen in the southern town of Kandahar and in neighbouring Pakistan denied the Kabul reports of battlefied gains and said the militia had killed 20 government fighters, taken more territory and shot down a helicopter.
A government helicopter was hit by Taleban artillery when trying to evacuate injured troops southwest of the capital Kabul and crashed, a Taleban spokesman said.
A government spokesman, Amrullah, earlier said in Kabul government forces had captured five important mountaintops near the Taleban-held Maidan Shahr town, southwest of Kabul.
But Kabul Radio, monitored in the Pakistani capital Islamabad at night, said eight Taleban posts were taken.
"Sher Ali mountain top, overlooking Maidan Shahr, came under our control today, after we launched a counter-attack on the Taleban after two days of sporadic clashes," Amrullah said.
The Taleban, entrenched in hills south of Kabul for the past year, have sworn to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose strict Islamic rule throughout Afghanistan.

Amrullah said the government was ready to negotiate peace with Taleban at any time. "When we talk about negotiations, it is not an indication of weakness," he said. "We are able to defend our forces and territories."

In turn, Taleban sources in Pakistan said the militia had captured more territory in Logar province after taking the strategic Azra district there on Friday. There was no independent confirmation of reports from either side.

However, Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's office in Kabul confirmed the fall of Azra, southeast of Kabul, which military analysts say could become a staging post for the Taleban to attack the strategic eastern town of Sarobi and the neutrally-administered eastern province of Nangarhar.

A spokesman for Hekmatyar said forces commanded by a neutral council ruling Nangarhar were fighting on the government side against the advancing Taleban forces in the province's Hisarak district. There was no immediate confirmation of this from independent sources.
A Pakistan-based Afghan news service said four pro-government fighters were killed and six wounded when their vehicle struck a landmine in Hisarak district on Saturday.

The Afghan Islamic Press service also quoted a Taleban spokesman as saying government forces had "completely failed in the battlefield" in their offensive towards Maidan Shahr and fled leaving 20 dead.
Another Taleban spokesman in the southern town of Kandahar, Mullah Mutaqi, said government forces succeeded in breaching a militia frontline southwest of Kabul but were later repulsed.
